items.title: Buckingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2019
items.q: by that time I had told Dolly that Larry Welk’s offered me this job to do Vanguard.

ctx.x: Well I’ll tell you how that all came about. I was with Columbia Records for ten, eleven, twelve years. VP of A&R. And then that was when CBS, Columbia and Epic, and I think it was around 1989 Sony bought Columbia and Epic from CBS. And I stayed on. And then — I can’t remember exactly the year, I want to say ’97, ’96, ’95, ’96, Sony approached Dolly about doing her own imprint (this will lead to “Spirituals to Swing” believe it or not), her own imprint label. And she called it Blue Eye Records. So the records from…

great artist, no matter what, even the political backlash in the 50s, it was Vanguard. I said I’d do the same thing the Solomon Brothers do. Just find great artists no matter what the genre and make it an artist-friendly label. And he called me and he called me and picked my brain. And I remember getting off the phone one day and I remember telling my assistant then, Jenny, I said, “I think he’s going to offer me a job.” And she said, “What would you do?” I said, “I would take it and you would do it with me.…
